blocks.orig: 10 DAYS SAFARI MKOMAZI + USAMBARA MOUNTAINS + SAADANI WITH BEACH RELAXATION
blocks.html: 10-day safari to Mkomazi, the Usambara Mountains and Saadani, ending with beach time

blocks.orig: This is a perfect safari combination to see the eastern parks of Tanzania. And you can end the safari with some relaxation on the beach.
blocks.html: This combination is an ideal way to discover Tanzania’s eastern parks, and you can round off the safari by unwinding on the beach.

blocks.orig: Mkomazi National Park is a truly spectacular wilderness and is located on the southern tip of the Sahel. It provides a home for herds of elephants, oryx and zebras. The Usambara Mountains are one of the undiscovered places in Tanzania. This is what makes this place a true paradise for nature and hiking lovers. And Saadani National Park has a unique location because it is on the coast. It is the only national park where you can combine an adventure safari with a relaxing stay at beautiful white beaches with many palm trees.
blocks.html: On the southern edge of the Sahel lies Mkomazi National Park, a genuinely spectacular wilderness that is home to herds of elephants, oryx and zebras. The Usambara Mountains remain one of Tanzania’s undiscovered corners, which makes them a real paradise for anyone who loves nature and hiking. Saadani National Park, meanwhile, is unusual in that it sits on the coast. No other national park lets you pair an adventurous safari with a relaxing stay on lovely white beaches lined with palm trees.

blocks.orig: This private safari offers you the flexibility to travel at your own pace, exactly the way you like it. You will have a private safari vehicle and guide. The hotels we selected for you during this safari are Silver class.
blocks.html: Because this safari is private, you can travel at your own pace and exactly as you prefer. A safari vehicle and guide are reserved just for you. For this safari we have chosen hotels in the Silver class.

blocks.orig: Many travelers ask us when the best time is to visit Tanzania. The answer is … there is not one right answer. It depends on what you want to see, where you want to go, your budget and interests. Please find a comprehensive guide on when is the best time to visit Tanzania here.
blocks.html: Travellers often ask us when they should visit Tanzania. The truth is that no single answer is right. It all depends on what you want to see, where you plan to go, your budget and your interests. Take a look at our detailed guide on the best time to visit Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Our safaris in Tanzania offer an opportunity to explore the country’s incredible wildlife and stunning landscapes. We specialize in private safaris, which means you have a 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep all to yourselves. You have the flexibility to decide when the safari starts and ends, and our experienced guides can help you make that decision on the day of your adventure. Whether you want to witness the animals at their most active during sunrise and sunset when temperatures are pleasant, or if you fancy ending the day by the pool, it’s entirely up to you. Tanzania’s diverse wildlife is active at various times of the day, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to spot the animals in action.
blocks.html: A safari with us in Tanzania lets you explore the country’s extraordinary wildlife and beautiful landscapes. We focus on private safaris, so you have a 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep entirely to yourselves. It’s up to you when the safari begins and finishes, and our experienced guides can help you choose on the day. You might want to see the animals at their liveliest around sunrise and sunset, when it’s pleasantly cool, or you might prefer to end the day at the pool; you decide. Tanzania’s wildlife is active at different moments throughout the day, so there will be plenty of chances to watch animals in action.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is renowned as one of the prime destinations to encounter the Big Five. These magnificent creatures—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo—can be observed in their natural habitats, making Tanzania a preferred choice for wildlife enthusiasts.
blocks.html: Certainly. Tanzania is famous as one of the top destinations for seeing the Big Five. Lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo all live here in their natural habitats, which makes Tanzania a favourite with wildlife enthusiasts.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is a safe and welcoming destination for travelers. The country offers a hospitable environment, especially in tourist areas like Arusha, and you can explore its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with confidence. Local people are friendly, and safety measures, such as keeping an eye on your belongings, are always advisable, just as you would in any other part of the world. Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people make it a fantastic place to visit.
blocks.html: Certainly. Tanzania is a safe and welcoming country for travellers. It offers a hospitable atmosphere, above all in tourist areas such as Arusha, so you can explore its landscapes and wildlife with confidence. The local people are friendly, and taking the usual precautions, such as watching your belongings, is always a good idea, as it would be anywhere in the world. Its natural beauty and the warmth of its people make Tanzania a fantastic destination.

blocks.orig: Mkomazi National Park is 3200 square kilometers in size and lies in the north of Tanzania, close to Moshi and the border with Kenya. Together with Kenya's Tsavo National Park, it provides a base for migratory herds of elephants, oryx and zebras during the rainy season. Visitors cannot miss the Mbula Rhino Sanctuary where rhinos might come close to the car! During regular game drives, you usually encounter animals such as giraffes, antelopes, buffalos, lions, leopards and many more.
blocks.html: Covering 3200 square kilometres, Mkomazi National Park lies in northern Tanzania, near Moshi and the Kenyan border. Along with Kenya's Tsavo National Park, it serves as a base for migrating herds of elephants, oryx and zebras in the rainy season. The Mbula Rhino Sanctuary is a must for visitors, and the rhinos may come right up to the car! On the regular game drives you’ll usually see animals such as giraffes, antelopes, buffalos, lions, leopards and many others.

blocks.orig: The Mbula Rhino Sanctuary lies within the boundaries of Mkomazi National Park, where it is home to over 35 rhinos, and their numbers are growing. The rhinos were reintroduced to Mkomazi in the 1990s and visitors can enter the sanctuary in an open safari vehicle of the national park, together with a ranger. This ranger knows precisely where the rhinos are and will do his best to arrange an encounter. Don't be surprised if these majestic animals walk straight to your car!
blocks.html: Inside the boundaries of Mkomazi National Park, the Mbula Rhino Sanctuary is home to more than 35 rhinos, and the population is increasing. The rhinos were brought back to Mkomazi in the 1990s, and you can visit the sanctuary with a ranger in one of the national park’s open safari vehicles. The ranger knows exactly where to find the rhinos and will do his utmost to arrange a sighting. Don't be surprised if these impressive animals walk right up to your car!

blocks.orig: The Usambara Mountains are a lush green mountain range south of Mkomazi National Park, with a cool climate that is ideal for hikes. Walks take you over sweeping hills, along waterfalls, farmland, plantations, picturesque villages and colourful markets, with the most amazing views almost everywhere you go. During the hike with a guide, you will see all sorts of flowers, butterflies, chameleons, and fruit trees and enjoy the view over the outstretched plains just beyond these mountains. You sleep in one of the area's highest hotels: Mambo View Point.
blocks.html: South of Mkomazi National Park, the Usambara Mountains form a lush green range whose cool climate is perfect for hiking. Your walks lead over rolling hills, past waterfalls, farmland, plantations, picturesque villages and colourful markets, with wonderful views at almost every turn. Walking with a guide, you’ll come across all kinds of flowers, butterflies, chameleons and fruit trees, and look out over the wide plains just beyond the mountains. You spend the night at Mambo View Point, one of the highest hotels in the area.

blocks.orig: The Magoroto Forest Estate lies 850 meters above sea level and is part of the Eastern Usambara Mountains. It’s known for its beautiful campground near an amazingly still freshwater lake surrounded by dense tropical rainforests. On your first day, you hike along one of Magoroto’s hiking trails to the waterfalls. The day after you entertain yourself with activities such as boat rides, swimming, fishing, bird watching, hiking, horse riding, or mountain biking!
blocks.html: At 850 metres above sea level, the Magoroto Forest Estate is part of the Eastern Usambara Mountains. It is known for a lovely campsite beside a wonderfully calm freshwater lake, surrounded by dense tropical rainforest. On the first day you follow one of Magoroto’s hiking trails to the waterfalls. The next day you keep yourself busy with activities like boat rides, swimming, fishing, birdwatching, hiking, horse riding or mountain biking!

blocks.orig: Saadani National Park is a small national park on the coast between Dar es Salaam and Tanga. It's the only national park on the coast of East Africa and the only place where you go on safari during the day, only to relax in a tropical beach setting afterward. Spot waterbucks, gazelles, giraffes, warthogs, hippos, crocodiles, baboons, and, with a bit more luck, elephants, lions, and leopards during the safari by car, on foot, or by boat!
blocks.html: Between Dar es Salaam and Tanga lies Saadani National Park, a small park on the coast. It is the only coastal national park in East Africa and the only place where you can go on safari by day and then relax on a tropical beach afterwards. On safari by car, on foot or by boat you can spot waterbucks, gazelles, giraffes, warthogs, hippos, crocodiles, baboons and, if you’re a little luckier, elephants, lions and leopards!

blocks.orig: The last day! Enjoy the final moments of your holiday before heading to Julius Nyerere International Airport in Dar Es Salaam for your flight home. Having second thoughts? Extending your holiday to paradise islands, such as Zanzibar, Pemba, or Mafia is also possible!
blocks.html: Your final day! Make the most of the last moments of your holiday before you travel to Julius Nyerere International Airport in Dar Es Salaam for your flight home. Not quite ready to leave? You can also extend your holiday to island paradises such as Zanzibar, Pemba or Mafia!
